results.title: Japan to declare aim to become AI leader after US, China
results.description: TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Japan will declare its aim to become a leading artificial intelligence nation after the United States and China, it was learned Wednesday. The government will include this goal when it revises the country's three key national security documents later this year. On Wednesday, the government presented an outline of the economic security sections of the revised documents at a meeting of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party and obtained broad approval. According to the outline, the revised documents will call for reducing Japan's AI reliance on other countries, noting that diplomacy and national defense will depend on economic and technological capabilities. The revised documents will also include plans to invest intensively in automated driving and physical AI technologies, as well as the goal of acquiring a technological advantage that renders Japan indispensable to other countries. Under the revised documents, Japan will conduct risk assessments for energy, food, medical and other strategic goods and strengthen supply chains through collaboration with reliable countries and regions. The government will increase state support where economic rationality prevents stable supplies. The revised documents will emphasize the need for a fair and predictable international economic order that is not affected by economic coercion, apparently referring to China's export restrictions. They will also call for establishing collective resilience by advancing the Free and Open Indo-Pacific vision.

results.title: Over 18,000 homebuyers secure homes through Pag-IBIG Fund Acquired Assets in 10 months, up 55%
results.description: A total of 18,071 homes were secured by Filipino homebuyers and their families through the Pag-IBIG Fund Acquired Assets Program from January to October 2026, an increase of 55 percent from the 11,664 homes acquired during the same period last year, as the agency continued to make homeownership more accessible and affordable under the government's Expanded Pambansang Pabahay para sa Pilipino (Expanded 4PH) Program. More aspiring homebuyers can take advantage of discounts of up to 30 percent on Pag-IBIG Fund Acquired Assets nationwide through the ongoing Acquired Assets Super Sale Part 2, which runs from Sept. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026. The initiative builds on the success of the first Super Sale launched in August 2025. Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development Secretary and Pag-IBIG Fund Board Chairman Jose Ramon P. Aliling said the Acquired Assets Program is among the diverse housing modalities under Expanded 4PH, reflecting the government's comprehensive approach to addressing the country's housing needs. "Our comprehensive approach under Expanded 4PH goes beyond expanding the supply of new homes. It also includes making existing housing inventory more accessible and affordable through programs such as Pag-IBIG Fund's Acquired Assets, one of the many housing options we are making available to Filipino families. By providing diverse pathways to homeownership, we are extending opportunities to families across income groups, including those who have long aspired to secure ownership of the homes where they live. This is in keeping with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.'s vision of enabling more Filipino families to lead better, more secure lives through homeownership," Aliling said. The homes acquired during the ten-month period had a combined sales value of ₱25.23 billion, up 74 percent from ₱14.53 billion in the same period last year, with an average purchase price of approximately ₱1.40 million per property. Aside from cash and short-term installment options, qualified homebuyers may purchase these properties through a Pag-IBIG Housing Loan, allowing them to further benefit from affordable interest rates and repayment terms of up to 30 years, making monthly payments more manageable. Pag-IBIG Fund also offers its Lease with Option to Purchase Program to qualified occupants of its Acquired Assets who are not yet financially ready to purchase the properties they occupy. The program allows them to legitimize their tenure through a lease arrangement while providing a pathway toward eventual ownership of their homes. Pag-IBIG Fund Chief Executive Officer Marilene C. Acosta emphasized how the Acquired Assets Program expands homeownership opportunities while contributing to the growth of members' savings. "We want our members to know that our Acquired Assets offer another affordable way for them to become homeowners. With the discounts we offer and our affordable financing options, members can find homes that suit their needs and budgets, whether they are looking for their first home or seeking to finally own the property where their families have been living. Every home acquired through this program also enables us to recover funds that we can use to finance more homes for our members, while generating earnings that help us grow the savings of our entire membership through annual dividends," Acosta said. Interested homebuyers may explore available properties, create their Buyer ID and participate in online bidding through the Acquired Assets section of the official Pag-IBIG Fund website at http://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph.
